To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lung microcirculatory barrier is not damaged by prolonged ECMO in the unanesthetised animal, and that total pulmonary blood flow does not influence the net filtration of fluid across the lung microvasculature.

prolonged partial VV and VA bypass with a filler-free silicone spiral coil membrane lung does not affect lung microvascular permeability, lung water content, or net fluid filtration across lung capillaries.

the permeability properties of the pulmonary capillary endothelium are not altered during prolonged partial Veno-Arterial or Veno-Venous bypass with a membrane oxygenator, and that the net fluid filtration across lung capillaries in the unanesthetize lambs is independent of the total pulmonary blood flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of prolonged extracorporeal circulation on the steady-state lung transvascular fluid dynamics.
the effect of extracorporeal circulation on lung water dynamics in unanesthethized lambs.
the use of extracorporeal life support (ECLS) as a bridge to lung transplantation in the treatment of acute lung injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a membrane lung does not alter the steady state of lung transcapillary water and protein exchange in the unanesthetised lamb.
ECMO has no effect on the steady-state lung fluid dynamics.
the use of ECMO does not alter lung transcapillary filtration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lung microvasculature is remarkably resistant to changes in flow, and this resistance may be a key factor in the maintenance of lung fluid homeostasis.

lung fluid balance during prolonged partial bypass with membrane lungs is not altered by the presence of an external circuit, and that lung fluid balance is not altered by a reduction in total lung perfusion.

ECMO does not appear to affect the steady-state dynamics in the lung microcirculatory bed, and thus ECMO may be a viable alternative to conventional mechanical ventilation in some patients with respiratory failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ECMO does not cause lung edema.
the lungs are not harmed by prolonged use of ECMOVV bypass in unanesthitzed lambs.
the lung is a robust organ and that the use of membrane oxygenator support for prolonged periods of time does not appear to have a significant effect on lung fluid dynamics.
